risk_reasons: The edit is inside the response-persist transaction on the worker — the path that must never break; a fault there stops draft generation for an account.
It changes the auto-approval Refusal lane (policy_gate_held), which is autonomy-adjacent surface.
The change makes a documented containment lever actually contain; a wrong fix leaves operators trusting a lever that still does nothing.
goal: With REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED off, no Refusal ledger code path can throw into the response-persist transaction, and any ledger throw on the policy_gate_held lane is attributed to subsystem 'refusal_ledger'.
non_goals: Do not edit src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts — the precedence totality hole is #1080 and runs in a sibling worktree in this same wave.
Do not extend attribution to the other six write sites — that is #1083 and lands in a later wave.
Do not change the resolver's throw semantics; an unmapped or unranked code stays a fault with the flag on.
Do not swallow a ledger error on the policy_gate_held or held_draft lane with the flag on — a draft must never commit without its Refusal row.
Do not batch, reorder, or otherwise restructure the ledger writes.
user_visible_behavior: Operational: with REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false, a ResponseGeneratorWorker job whose gate decision would resolve an unmapped or unranked block reason persists its draft and completes, instead of aborting and burning its attempts.
Operational: with the flag on, a resolver throw raises a Sentry issue tagged subsystem=refusal_ledger and refusal_lane=policy_gate_held, naming the flag, instead of a generic worker_job failure.

Operational: the once-per-episode 'ledger is dark' warning still fires on every lane, policy_gate_held included. That lane no longer reaches a write arm with the flag off, so it raises the same line explicitly via noteRefusalLedgerDark, and only when every block reason maps to a real category — the condition under which a row would genuinely have been recorded.
invariants: src/lib/refusals/write.ts stays the single WRITE-PATH owner of the REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED read; persist.ts never re-spells readFlagEnabledByDefault(REFUSAL_LEDGER_FLAG).
src/app/api/dashboard/refusals/route.ts:76 is a deliberate READ-path second reader that must keep its own literal flag spelling for ci:env-registry; it is out of surface and must not be 'fixed'.

isRefusalLedgerEnabled is SIDE-EFFECT-FREE: it reads the flag and returns; it never warns, never clears the disabled episode, and never logs. The word is not 'pure' — vocabulary.ts defines that for this area as excluding a flag read.
noteRefusalLedgerDark is the side-effecting sibling and calls the SAME private warnLedgerDisabled, so it shares the once-per-episode latch and cooldown rather than adding a second signal.
wouldRecordRefusal uses every, never some: one null-mapped member vetoes the whole row (#1003), so some would warn about a decision that was never going to be recorded.
warnLedgerDisabled and endDisabledEpisode stay private to write.ts and stay inside writeRefusalEvent and writeRefusalEvents, unmoved.
The flag read stays live and per call — never a module-scope const, so a mid-process toggle is observed (the rule circuit-breaker.ts states).
writeRefusalEvents keeps its empty-input return BEFORE the flag read; an empty set has no ledger gap to warn about.
With the flag on, both persist write sites stay uncaught: a migration-116 CHECK violation is a writer bug and must abort the transaction.
withLedgerAttribution still changes no control flow — it captures, then rethrows the SAME error instance, and a failing reporter never replaces the real error.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts remains the only production module that spells INSERT INTO refusal_events.
With the flag off, the persist transaction invokes the refusals vocabulary resolver ZERO times on both lanes.
edge_cases: Flag off and the block-reason set is empty or fully null-mapped: the new flag guard returns before the resolver, so nothing is written, the transaction commits, and no disabled warning fires. The OUTCOME matches today's silence; the CAUSE differs — today guard 4 returns first, after the change the flag guard returns before guard 4 is reached.

Flag off and the set WOULD have resolved: the lane returns before the resolver, and wouldRecordRefusal is true, so noteRefusalLedgerDark raises the same once-per-episode line the write arms raise. The warning is preserved, not lost.

Flag off and one member is UNMAPPED: wouldRecordRefusal returns false, so no warning fires. Correct on the no-gap rule — an unmapped member would have thrown rather than written, so no row was lost — but it is a real blind spot for the #1080 fault class, recorded in docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md.
Flag on and the resolver returns null: no write, no Sentry capture, transaction commits — byte-identical to today.
Flag on and the resolver throws: captured exactly once with the lane tag, the SAME instance rethrown, transaction aborts — the designed behaviour.
The held_draft lane at persist.ts:877 has no pre-write resolve (every argument is a literal or the module constant HELD_DRAFT_REFUSAL_CATEGORY), so it gains no guard and no behaviour change.

Two live flag reads exist per write — the persist guard, then write.ts — but the window between them is ZERO, not microseconds: no await separates them, because withLedgerAttribution and writeRefusalEvent each run synchronously to their first await and the second read is writeRefusalEvent's first statement. A mid-process flip cannot land between them, so there is nothing to defend against and nothing for a test to exercise.

The guard docblock's recorded mutation result was re-measured per guard at #1079 and the old summary was wrong for two of three: deleting guard 1 kills this branch's own held_draft pin, guard 2 survives 82/82, and deleting guard 3 kills a pre-existing test AND writes a spurious policy_gate_held row. The docblock carries the per-guard numbers, not the summary sentence.

A zero-resolver-invocation assertion is an assertion of ABSENCE, so a wrong tier, a non-live-ingest origin lane, a null threshold, held=true or approved=true each make it pass on HEAD too. The same fixture with the flag ON must record exactly one invocation, or the test is a permanent false green.

rollback_plan: Revert the branch. The change adds no schema, no migration and no new column; REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED keeps its current default, so reverting restores exactly today's behaviour (the flag is ineffective again on this lane, which is the pre-change state).
observability: A Sentry issue tagged subsystem=refusal_ledger, refusal_lane=policy_gate_held distinguishes a ledger fault from a generic worker_job failure.

The once-per-episode ledger-dark warning is PRESERVED on this lane: guard 4's off-arm raises it through noteRefusalLedgerDark whenever wouldRecordRefusal is true. Review proved the earlier concession avoidable, and the branch closed it rather than shipping the gap.

REMAINING BLIND SPOT, narrowed but real: an UNMAPPED block reason (the #1080 fault class) raises nothing on this lane while the flag is off — it would have thrown rather than written, so wouldRecordRefusal is false and no row was lost, but no operator signal names it either. The Restraint tab's ledgerRecording disclaimer is what shows the ledger is off at all. Recorded in docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md so an operator meets it before an incident does.

That Sentry issue is the record of a vocabulary fault ONLY for a flag flipped in response to it. A fault arriving into an ALREADY-off flag never runs the resolver, so no issue is raised; and an operator who resolves the issue after the aborts stop removes the record while the flag stays off.
